properties.statement: `claim_region`'s OWN DESCRIPTION DESCRIBES THE PRE-`--shared` WORLD AS FACT, AND ITS `seat` PARAMETER DOCUMENTS A REFUSAL THAT DOES NOT HAPPEN. Reported three times across two weeks. (1) The description states the claim is 'only as fresh as the last pull, because the design lives as a file in each checkout WITH NO SHARED SERVER (dec:multi-writer-architecture)' — read by api-boss `5d608b85` while running exactly a shared server with 7 attached processes. THIS REPO CONFIRMS THE TEXT IS STILL SHIPPED: the CLAIMS edge hint in the schema reads 'the design lives as a file in each person's checkout with no shared server to hold a lock'. Both architectures are supported; the description asserts one of them as fact, so a session reading it in a `--shared` deployment builds a wrong mental model of what a claim even IS. (2) The `seat` parameter's docs say that on the SESSIONLESS transport a handler is built per request, so omitting `seat` 'is REFUSED rather than answered with a seat that would change on your next call'. w-10f94d47 omitted it. It was NOT refused — the call succeeded and the server returned `seat: "ajs77:2304014:0e0681c1"`. Either the behaviour changed or the transport there is not the sessionless one; either way the schema text and the behaviour disagree, and a reader who believes the schema will either mint a seat they did not need or read a success as a bug. They flagged it as not-blocking and reported it anyway because a silent workaround forfeits the fix. (3) w-8da9c31c reported on 2026-08-03 that the description still described the pre-`--shared` world. THE PATTERN THESE SIT IN, named by w-10f94d47: three version-dependent facts landed in copied instruction blocks in ONE DAY with no version stamp and no expiry — the served_by 0.22.1 literal, the mint_seat correction, and this schema note. Their suggestion: have the SERVER be the authority, stating 'as of 0.24.0' next to any tool-existence claim, so a copied doc can be CHECKED against the running binary instead of trusted. A doc that cannot be distinguished from a stale doc is indistinguishable from a wrong one.
